subject: marginal_effects() for nonlinear link functions in hierarchical models

messages.author: 1562416f5ac8e298
messages.subject: marginal_effects() for nonlinear link functions in hierarchical models
parts:
I have a question for the predictions / fitted values produced by marginal_effects() for hierarchical models with random effects and nonlinear link functions (e.g., mixed effects logistic regression): Namely, in the help page of the function it is mentioned that when re_formula = NA (default), then marginal predictions are calculated. Does this mean that only the fixed-effects part of the model is used? For nonlinear link functions this wouldn’t correspond to marginal predictions, right?

Thanks for any pointers!

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] marginal_effects() for nonlinear link functions in hierarchical models
parts:
Yes indeed, only the fixed effects are used, which in non-linear models is not identical to marginal predictions. Unfortunately, the latter are far more difficult to compute...

In retrospect, the name "marginal_effects" was suboptimal. See also my comment in the details section of ?marginal_effects
